builders.angle: THE KIT, EXACTLY. Every piece of kit.css has already been judged, and the most coherent candidate is usually the one that invents least. Build all three out of what exists: the coach note as a .kit-panel with its heading in .kit-heading and its two buttons as .kit-btn and .kit-btn--quiet, the spotlight drawn with the same gilt edge the kit's frames use; the veil as a staged board -- the next Kid in a .kit-frame over a .kit-plate, the Companion beside them, the I'm ready control a .kit-btn with its medallion -- on a painted ground that hides the fight entirely; the toast as a .kit-enamel or .kit-plate plaque whose rim is the tier's metal, moved clear of the Companion's portrait. Add a class only where the kit truly has nothing, and say which in notes_for_merger.

THINGS IN THE HOUSE. Make each piece an object that could exist in this mansion rather than a panel that floats over it. The coach is a note in Marmalade's hand -- a card, a torn page, a luggage tag -- held by something (a brass tack, a ribbon, propped on a candle), and the spotlight is a pool of candlelight rather than an outlined box. The veil is something drawn across the room: heavy velvet curtains, a door, a folding screen, with the next Kid's portrait hung or pinned on it and their Companion waiting. The toast is a medal on a ribbon, or a rosette, whose metal IS the tier. Every object must still keep its contract from the brief -- the note never covers what it points at, the veil hides the board completely, the toast stays off the HUD -- and every object must sit in the kit's palette, not in the colour of the real material (round 6's warning).

CEREMONY, AND THE TYPE FIRST. These three are mostly words, and the samples' strongest device is the title cartouche: engraved serif display, a gold ribbon with star glyphs, spaced small caps. Lead with typography and ceremony: the veil is a title card -- the next Kid's name set the way title.png sets MIDNIGHT MENAGERIE, their portrait and Companion staged under it, PASS IT OVER on a ribbon -- because handing the machine across is a small ceremony between two people on a sofa; the toast is a ribbon banner unfurling with the achievement's name, the tier as the medallion that pins it; the coach is Marmalade speaking, her portrait in a medallion beside a speech plate, with the type hierarchy of the samples rather than a paragraph in a box. Check every word at 1280x800.
